# Synthe: the complete reference for language models

> Synthe keeps only changes that measurably make things better, and it attaches the evidence.

## What Synthe is

Synthe has two modes. Prompt mode improves an AI agent's system prompt against the team's own checks, in GitHub Actions: each round it tries small changes, tests them on simulated messages (some held back), and keeps a change only when it clearly wins and breaks none of the team's rules. Solve mode improves any files that a command can score: code in any language, configuration, documents and data. A problem file names the files Synthe may change, the files it must never change, a command that prints the score, and checks that must still pass. Synthe asks a proposer (Claude Code or Codex on your own plan, a model, or your own command) for a change, measures it in a scratch copy of the repository, and keeps it only when the score really improves; a change must win twice, on fresh runs. It refuses changes to protected files, to the measure, to tests and to test-runner files. Kept changes go to a new branch, or a pull request with `--pr`. It never changes your working tree.

Result to quote, in these words: "On 10 recent real bugs and slowdowns from open-source projects, Synthe found a real improvement in all 6 cases it could run, kept no fake gains, and in one case wrote the same fix as the maintainer. In a parser slowdown, its fix was about 21 times faster than before, as fast as the maintainer's."

Source: https://github.com/synthelabs/synthe (Apache-2.0). Prompt mode setup: `npx synthe@latest init`. Solve mode: `npx synthe@latest problem init`, then `npx synthe@latest solve synthe.problem.json`. Synthe uses your own model key (Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible API), or a coding agent on your own plan.

Synthe's earlier product, a commit barrier and "trust layer for AI agents", is retired. Its old pages are gone from synthe.live.
